title: Studying in Italy: a complete guide from scratch
lead: Start here even if you know nothing. This page explains the whole path in plain language: from choosing a university to becoming a full student in Italy.

overview.title: 1. The university admits you
overview.text: You apply on the university's own portal. If the answer is positive, you receive a pre-acceptance letter.

overview.title: 2. The Italian state gives permission
overview.text: Your diploma is recognised (DoV or CIMEA), you do the pre-enrollment on Universitaly and get a type D student visa from the embassy in Tashkent.

overview.title: 3. You complete the formalities in Italy
overview.text: Within 8 days of arrival you apply for the residence permit (permesso di soggiorno), get a codice fiscale and fully register at the university (full enrollment).

overview.title: In parallel: the scholarship
overview.text: Italian regions give students from low-income families a scholarship of more than 7 171 € a year, free meals and a tuition fee waiver. You apply in summer while you are still in Uzbekistan.

timeline.title: Set your goal
timeline.text: Choose your level (bachelor's or master's), field and 3–5 universities. Bring your English up to B2 (IELTS 5.5–6.5, depending on the programme). Your passport should be valid for at least 2 years.

timeline.title: University application (pre-acceptance)
timeline.text: Each university has its own portal and deadline. Many universities open applications in autumn or winter: for example Padova for 2027/28 on 15.09–15.11.2026 and 01.12.2026–01.03.2027. The application fee is usually 10–30 €.

timeline.title: Diploma recognition: DoV or CIMEA
timeline.text: You get an apostille on your school certificate or diploma and have it translated. Then you get a DoV from the embassy or apply online to CIMEA. CIMEA takes up to 60 working days, so do not delay.

timeline.title: Pre-enrollment on Universitaly
timeline.text: On the Italian Ministry of Education's portal you apply for your chosen programme. The university confirms it and sends it to the embassy. Each university has its own deadline (in 2026/27 they ranged from 30.06 to 15.09).

timeline.title: Scholarship application (DSU)
timeline.text: You apply to the agency of the region where your university is. For this you need family documents: family composition, income, property. You prepare them in Uzbekistan with apostille and translation.

timeline.title: Student visa
timeline.text: You apply at the consular section of the Italian Embassy in Tashkent. Processing takes up to 90 days. You show {{viza}} per year on a legal, traceable account, yours or your family's.

timeline.title: Getting ready for the trip
timeline.text: Insurance of at least 30 000 € for the whole Schengen area, a ticket, accommodation for the first month. Take the originals and translations of all documents with you.

timeline.title: Permesso di soggiorno and codice fiscale
timeline.text: You pick up the kit at a post office marked «Sportello Amico» and apply for the permesso. Also get a codice fiscale (tax code), an Italian SIM card and a bank account: the scholarship is paid into it.

timeline.title: Full enrollment and ISEE
timeline.text: You hand in your original documents to the university and complete full registration. For the scholarship you get an ISEE parificato at a CAF centre. The list of results (graduatoria) is published.

timeline.title: Renewal
timeline.text: You renew the permesso before it expires. You reapply for the scholarship every year: from the second year you must have earned enough CFU (credits).

levels.title: 11-year school certificate
levels.text: A bachelor's degree in Italy usually requires 12 years of schooling. There are two ways: a Foundation year (at Sapienza, Pavia, Padova, Messina and others; see the «Foundation» page) or studying for 1 year at a university in Uzbekistan and then applying.

levels.title: 12 years of schooling or 1st year of university
levels.text: You can apply directly for a bachelor's degree (laurea triennale, 3 years). Many programmes ask for a SAT or CEnT-S result.

levels.title: Bachelor's degree
levels.text: You apply for a master's degree (laurea magistrale, 2 years). Your bachelor's subjects must match the chosen master's. Many programmes have a minimum GPA.

levels.title: Medicine
levels.text: Admission to medicine (Medicine and Surgery) programmes follows a separate procedure with limited places. The procedure has changed in recent years, so check the university's bando every year.

glossary.def: The university's answer «we are ready to admit you». You cannot apply for the visa without it.
A 1-year preparatory course for those who finished 11-year school. It completes the right to enter a bachelor's degree.
Bachelor's: 3 years, 180 CFU.
Master's: 2 years, 120 CFU.
A 5–6 year single-cycle programme: medicine, law, architecture and others.
The Italian credit unit (the same as ECTS). One academic year is 60 CFU.
A stamp confirming a document's authenticity. Uzbekistan is a party to the Hague Convention, so an apostille is enough.
A document issued by the embassy: it states what your diploma is equivalent to in Italy.
An Italian centre that verifies diplomas online. It issues Comparability (equivalence) and Verification (authenticity) certificates.
The portal of the Italian Ministry of Education (MUR). Students who need a visa do their pre-enrollment here.
The application on Universitaly. Once the university confirms it, it goes to the embassy.
Student visa: 91 to 365 days, multiple entry. You cannot enrol for study on a tourist visa.
Residence permit in Italy. Requested within 8 days of arrival.
The police immigration office. It issues the permesso and takes fingerprints.
Italian tax code. Needed for the bank, phone, rent and the scholarship.
Diritto allo Studio Universitario: the regional scholarship and services (money, meals, accommodation, fee waiver).
Official call: a document setting out conditions, amounts and deadlines.
A document that converts a foreign student's family income and assets to the Italian system. The scholarship is based on it.
A citizens' service centre. This is where you get your ISEE parificato.
A student living away from their family. Receives the largest scholarship.
The list of results. Vincitore: winner, receives the scholarship. Idoneo: eligible, but funds ran out.
Immatricolazione: final registration. Original documents are handed in here.
Italian digital identity and official email. Some scholarship portals ask for them.

budget.note: At state universities (Sapienza 30 €, Unical and Politecnica delle Marche 10 €). At private ones 100 – 150 € (Bocconi 100 €, LUISS 150 €).
Fast track +100 €. If you choose DoV, according to the embassy's procedure.
The price depends on the number of documents and the translator. Have the translation done by a translator on the embassy's list.

budget.item: Proof of funds for the visa
budget.note: The 2026/27 requirement. This money is not spent: you show that it is in your account (or your sponsor's). In 2025/26 it was 6 947,33 €.
For the whole Schengen area and the whole period.
A 16 € marca da bollo, plus postal and card fees. The exact amount is written in the post office kit.
At state universities it is calculated from family income (ISEE). Scholarship winners are exempt from tuition fees.

mistakes: Applying to only one university. Apply to 3–5: their deadlines differ.
Waiting for the last day. Portals slow down, and CIMEA takes up to 60 working days.
Using different emails. Letters from the university, Universitaly and the embassy should go to one address.
Getting the bank statement too early. On the day you apply it must not be older than 10 working days.
Looking for family documents for the scholarship after arriving in Italy. Prepare them in Uzbekistan, with apostille and translation.
Delaying the permesso after arrival. You must apply within 8 days.
